
== Dancing Plague of 1518

In July of 1518, in Strasbourg, France, a woman began a dancing craze in a narrow street that lasted for 4-6 days. The crowd swelled to over 400 others by the end of the week. Most of them died due to strokes, heart attacks and exhaustion due to nonstop "jigging". It has stumped scientists for centuries about the cause for the plague. Theories suggest physcological stress from frozen winters and scorching summers, while others suggest the cause to be worry from the curse of St. Vigil, who plagued those who envoked his wrath with nonstop dancing. Several other cases of such outbursts have occurs worldwide, such as the Tanganyika Laughter Epidemic of 1962.<ref>http://dsc.discovery.com/news/2008/08/01/dancing-death-mystery.html</ref>
